cd /workspace && rm -rf /workspace/tmp/epic-build-* /workspace/tmp/sub /workspace/tmp/t /workspace/tmp/tb /workspace/tmp/tb2 && cat > /workspace/project/README.md <<'EOF'
# Offline EPIC collective collector

Finite four-port packet replay with exact wire and buffer certificates, as
specified by `../PROTOCOL.md`. Everything runs offline on the CPU: no NIC,
switch, GPU or external service is contacted.

## Layout

| Path | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `solver.py` | JSON stdin/stdout entry point. Validates the batch, encodes each case into a compact program, builds the C project into scratch once per invocation, replays every case and serializes certificates. |
| `request.py` | Public format-only request validator and expansion accounting (no collector logic). |
| `wire.py` | Public wire-format utility: canonical frame sealing, IPv4/ICRC checksums and event shorthand expansion. |
| `src/roce_packet.c` | Supplied RoCEv2 codec: frame parsing/sealing, IPv4 checksum, reflected CRC32 ICRC, primitive/mode names. |
| `src/star4_switch.c` | Supplied four-port live switch substrate, retained for its real collective and transport behaviour. |
| `src/collector.c` | Offline replay engine: strict wire acceptance, endpoint classification, bounded retention, cumulative ACKs, mode 2/mode 3 reliability translation, emission priority, local egress backpressure, FNV1a64 buffer digest, SHA-256 transcript and snapshots. |
| `src/replay_api.c` | Offline transport ABI surface (`include/offline_api.h`). |
| `include/` | Shared headers: codec declarations, replay ABI, offline port shim. |

## Pipeline

1. `request.py.load` validates the whole batch first; anything illegal answers
   exactly `{"error":"invalid"}` with exit status zero and no compilation.
2. `solver.py` encodes each case's events (data/ack/wire/budget/flush/retry/
   snap/train) into a little-endian program blob. No collector semantics live in
   Python.
3. `src/collector.c` replays the blob: it generates canonical ingress frames
   with the supplied codec, classifies every frame (wire-invalid,
   endpoint-invalid, accepted DATA/ACK, newly accepted, duplicate, blocked,
   stale, ignored ACK), maintains the retention window `[b, min(K,b+N))`, the
   received/eligible/upstream and sent/acknowledged prefixes, and performs the
   documented service opportunity after every endpoint-valid input packet and on
   flush/retry.
4. Certificates (state, buffer digest, transcript SHA-256, packets, bytes,
   snapshots, trace) come back as one binary blob per case and are serialized to
   JSON.

## Build and run

From `/workspace`, as the ordinary candidate user:

```
make -C project BUILD="$TMPDIR/manual-build" -j2
python3 -I -B project/solver.py < sample-request.json
python3 public_check.py project/solver.py
```

`solver.py` compiles into `$TMPDIR` (scratch) by itself and removes the build
directory afterwards; nothing is written next to the read-only sources. GCC,
GNU make, binutils and libc development headers are the only requirements.
